There is no driver admission in the chat log: the driver's only message says he is going by the KPE, which is the corridor the platform's own optimal route uses - optimal_route_source reads 'optimal is KPE then ECP, crossing both gantries'. erp_gantries is null, so no charged gantry places the vehicle on a corridor the optimal route does not use. The counterparty statement asserts the same KPE route and admits nothing. And trip_record.actual_distance_km is, on the pre-pass's own assessment, derived from this very trace, so it is not independent corroboration. The chat log is itself impaired at weight 0.6 with issue TRUNCATED_LOG (last message 18:26:14, 2,186 s before the trip ended); I do not assert what was said after that point. Without an independent source the claimed refund cannot be ordered.

The claim cites EV-FARE-00110 (weight_multiplier 0.75, issue PARTIAL_RECORD) and EV-GPS-00110 (weight_multiplier 0.39, issues GPS_GAP and LOW_COVERAGE) without stating that those artifacts are impaired or naming those issue codes; only EV-CHAT-00110's impairment is disclosed. A claim citing an impaired artifact in silence is discarded.

The trace is impaired - a 428.0 s gap and coverage of 81.7% - and no source in POL-RD-07(ii)'s list exists on this record. The one part of the route whose length decides this case is precisely the part this trace cannot measure, which is why the straight-line reconstruction is the driver-favourable reading POL-RD-07(i) mandates and not a finding about what was driven.

The admissibility note on EV-TRIP-00110 records that the figure is itself derived from the impaired trace and adds no independent evidence of distance, and the fare ledger's distance_charged_km is 21.20 as well. discarded_claims.reason: POL-GEN-02(1) disclosure failure. The claim cites EV-FARE-00110 (weight_multiplier 0.75, issue PARTIAL_RECORD) without stating that the artifact is impaired or naming its issue code.

POL-RD-10(3) makes escalation mandatory on the same facts. Under POL-GEN-03 an escalated amount is held rather than collected, so escalation is the outcome that leaves the rider not carrying the disputed charge.

ruling.explanation:
To both parties: this dispute turns on the one stretch of the trip that cannot be measured, so the case goes to a human reviewer and the disputed amount is held — neither collected nor refunded.

For the rider: the GPS trace for this trip (EV-GPS-00110) has a single 428-second gap in the KPE tunnel between 18:35:00 and 18:42:08, far over POL-RD-07's 90-second limb, and coverage of 81.7%. It is therefore impaired for POLICY purposes, not merely at the schema pre-pass, and it is down-weighted to 0.39 with issue codes GPS_GAP and LOW_COVERAGE. Measured the way POL-RD-07(i) requires — as the straight line between the bounding fixes, the reading most favourable to the driver — the trip is 21.2 km against a booked optimal of 18.4 km, an excess of 2.8 km (15.2%), which sits under POL-RD-01's 20% establishment gate, so no deviation is established on that reading. But POL-RD-07(ii) also forbids establishing a deviation on an impaired trace without an INDEPENDENT corroborating source, and there is none here: the chat log (EV-CHAT-00110, weight 0.60, issue TRUNCATED_LOG) contains no admission — the driver's only message names the KPE, which is the platform's own optimal corridor; the fare breakdown carries no gantry itemisation (EV-FARE-00110, weight 0.75, issue PARTIAL_RECORD), so no charged gantry places the vehicle off-corridor; the driver's statement asserts the same KPE corridor and concedes nothing; and the trip record's distance is itself derived from this trace, so it is not a second measurement. With the trace impaired and no POL-RD-07(ii) corroboration, POL-RD-07(iii) and POL-RD-10(3) make escalation mandatory rather than a finding for the driver: what is missing is proof, not a route. The finding rests on the impaired trace and survives its 0.39 discount — the impairment is the very reason for escalating, not a reason to prefer one reconstruction over the other — and confidence is capped at the trace's 0.39 (POL-GEN-02(2)), below the 0.70 platform floor, which is a further and independent escalation ground under POL-RD-10(1). The threshold is not merely missed, it is unmeasurable: a surface route between the same two portals would put the trip at 25.50 km and over the gate, and nothing in this bundle distinguishes the two readings.

For the driver: your account that you took the KPE is consistent with the platform's own optimal route (KPE then ECP), and the $3.00 ERP line is treated as matched — erp_gantries is null, so under POL-RD-09(4) the gantry match is undecidable on the record, the line stands, and no billing-integrity correction is made. Driver compensation under POL-RD-04 is not available either: distance_charged_km (21.20) does not fall short of the trace figure, so there is no unbilled distance.

No referral is issued. POL-RD-06(c) conduct review is not engaged: no material deviation arises on this trip, and the profile test the clause names returns no pattern (driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0). POL-RD-09(4) billing integrity is not engaged, for the reason above.

The impasse would be resolved by any of: an untruncated chat log covering the disputed window; an itemised ERP gantry list placing (or not placing) the vehicle on a different corridor; an LTA traffic advisory for the KPE/ECP in the 18:19–19:02 window; a trace without the tunnel dropout; or any rider-side track.
